answer: Texas uses electronic titles, so the title is a record at the state rather than a paper document, and your lender sends the lien release to the state electronically. The lien still has to be released, though: ask your lender for a lien release letter, or if you can't get one, sign the lien release request (form NW-LRL-1) and we'll contact the lender for you, which can add 1 to 2 weeks. We can still make you an offer and book your appointment while you wait, and once the lien is released we transfer the title electronically at the appointment.
